about: The parts of the terminal plugin's texts that thimble browser uses (server/thimble_browser/prompts.py). Each part is read from the plugin at run time: `file`, a file under plugin/, or `prompt`, a prompt of plugin/prompts/registry.mjs, read from its one file. Then a section of it and, when given, some of its bullets (counted from 1). `replace` and `drop` are the only changes, exact strings; tests/test_prompt_parity.py fails when the terminal's text no longer holds one of them.

In the reply, "heads" is null, or one heads-up, which the analyst opens as a short card: {"term": "<exact words from the answer>", "title": "<a few words>", "bullets": ["<a point, its words linked to the lines of a file that show it, where a file does>"], "todo": "<what to do>"}.

Read each text on its own. The answer is what the analyst reads now, and the report is what they share with others, so a detail that would change what they share needs its heads-up in the report, even when the answer has one.

In the reply, "heads" holds at most one heads-up for each text, and is often empty: [{"where": "<the text's place>", "term": "<exact words from that text>", "title": "<a few words>", "bullets": ["<a point, its words linked to the lines of a file that show it, where a file does>"], "todo": "<what to do>"}].
drop: Such details are often in the cards and in what the session read, at the end of this request. Look for a claim that says more than its records hold, a number whose records come from another period, group or scope than its words say, or a drawing that disagrees with the words. Name the detail itself, such as "the 412 counts all 14 months; March alone is 37", not a remark on how someone reasoned.
